note: An inline endpoint 55.000 m from its arc under SPEC 3.3.3, which a conforming reader must refuse, dropping the LINK per SPEC 6.2 - not the endpoint, which would leave a malformed link, and not the chain, which would be disproportionate. THE ARC RUNS NORTH TO SOUTH ON PURPOSE, and this is the least obvious property in the pair: do not 'tidy' it to match its ascending twin. A refusal case cannot catch a model that over-reads, because over-reading also refuses. Descending puts the segment start at high latitude and the query at low, so a reader taking the cosine of the segment's START latitude UNDER-reads it at 36.824 m and ACCEPTS A DOCUMENT THE FORMAT REFUSES. That is the more dangerous direction - a reader that silently accepts bad geometry is worse than one that complains about good geometry - and nothing else in the corpus covers it. THE THIRTEEN DEGREES ARE DELIBERATE for the same reason as the accept case: the error is a percentage and a realistic arc hides it. The expected message deliberately omits the measured distance, because the number a reader reports depends on its arithmetic and a conforming implementation differing in the last metre should not fail; what is pinned is that the endpoint was refused and the tolerance named.
